Investigations: Appreciate the importance of reviewing medications and allergies and documenting normal renal function before the use of contrast agents; explain significance of RBC casts, proteinuria and dysmorphic RBC in a patient with hematuria; when appropriate, tests may include: dipstick, urine microscopy and culture, CBC, urea and electrolytes, urine cytology, ultrasonography of abdomen and pelvis, IVU, CT, RGP, cystoscopy, ureterorenoscopy and biopsy.
Communication skills: Counsel and educate patients about drugs and foods that can cause red urine.
Procedure skills: Perform urine dipstick and interpret urine microscopy.

Management skills: Plan appropriate investigations to reveal the cause of hematuria depending on the clinical scenario and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the chosen modality; recognize the indications of referring the patient to a specialist (urologist/nephrologist).

Attitudes: Blood in urine is often very alarming for the patient and relatives; the physician should reassure the patient that serious disease is unlikely once the appropriate investigations are negative and hematuria has subsided.

topics.title: Urolithiasis
objectives: Knowledge: Explain why urolithiasis is endemic in Oman.
Knowledge: Identify the etiological factors for stone formation.
Knowledge: List the common types of urinary stones.
Knowledge: Discuss the common clinical presentations of urolithiasis.
Knowledge: Discuss the appropriate investigations to diagnose stone in different clinical scenarios.
Knowledge: Discuss the management of a patient with ureteric colic.
Knowledge: Plan appropriate treatment based on stone size, composition and location (conservative, medical expulsive therapy, medical dissolution therapy, ESWL, PCNL, ureteroscopy/pyelolithotomy).
Knowledge: Explain ESWL, PCNL, URS, cystolithotripsy, ureterolithotomy and pyelolithotomy.
Knowledge: Discuss the metabolic workup of a recurrent stone former.
Knowledge: Discuss the dietary advice to reduce stone recurrence.
Knowledge: Understand the importance of avoiding contrast media in renal failure.
Knowledge: Discuss the potential immediate complications on release of chronic obstruction.
History taking: Understand that proper history including dietary and family history is key to make the diagnosis; elicit history of renal/ureteric colic, lower urinary tract symptoms and infection.
Physical examination: Detect renal angle tenderness; exclude other causes of acute abdomen like dissecting aortic aneurysm and acute appendicitis.

Investigations: Know that although non-contrast CT (NCCT) has become the gold standard investigation for detection of ureteric calculi, there is radiation risk especially to ovaries and beware of cumulative radiation dose in recurrent stone formers.

Communication: Make patients aware of the importance of dietary discretion and increasing fluid intake to avoid stone recurrence; make patients with ureteric calculi aware of the need for close follow up to avoid renal injury.
Attitude: Be compassionate to patients with ureteric colic as it is one of the most painful diseases; beware of drug seekers presenting to the emergency department with spurious symptoms.

topics.title: Urinary incontinence
objectives: Knowledge: Define urinary incontinence.
Knowledge: Understand that urinary incontinence diminishes the quality of life but is underreported.
Knowledge: Discuss the receptors in the bladder and urethra.
Knowledge: Discuss the types of urinary incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss the pathophysiology of stress urinary incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss the pathophysiology of urge incontinence.
Knowledge: Define overactive bladder.
Knowledge: Discuss overflow incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss frequency volume chart.
Knowledge: Discuss evaluation of urinary incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss cough stress test.
Knowledge: Evaluate post void residual urine.
Knowledge: Discuss pelvic floor muscle training.
Knowledge: Discuss pharmacotherapy of urinary incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss surgical therapy of stress urinary incontinence (SUI).
Knowledge: Discuss mid urethral slings which are the new gold standard for treating SUI.
Knowledge: Discuss surgical therapy of urge incontinence.
Knowledge: Discuss the concept of clean intermittent catheterization (CIC).

History taking: Understand that proper history is key to differentiate between different types of urinary incontinence and that factors outside the urinary system like dementia or reduced mobility may be the cause; elicit dietary history and drug history that may impact urinary continence.

Physical examination: Do focused neurological examination to rule out neurological deficits; examine for palpable bladder; do DRE to assess anal tone, perianal sensation and prostate enlargement; demonstrate stress urinary incontinence; identify cystocele and uterine prolapse.
Differential diagnosis: Choose appropriate investigations for these patients.
Communication: Elicit voiding history and diet history; instruct patient to record frequency volume chart; give clear instructions for clean intermittent catheterization.

Attitude: Understand the importance of ensuring privacy during external genitalia examination and the need for a chaperone; understand that urinary incontinence has social stigma and often patients are hesitant to seek treatment.

topics.title: Problem-based seminar: scrotal swellings & pain
objectives: Discuss differential diagnosis of acute and chronic scrotal swellings and understand that proper history and focused clinical examination are key to differentiate between them.
Choose appropriate investigations for these patients and discuss the treatment of different scrotal swellings.
Understand the principles of evaluation and management of testicular tumors.
Obtain necessary consent for a patient undergoing scrotal surgery.

topics.title: Problem-based seminar: hematuria
objectives: Define microscopic hematuria.
Differentiate between glomerular and extraglomerular causes of hematuria.
Discuss the common causes of hematuria.
Identify risk factors for urological cancers.
Plan the diagnostic workup of a patient with painless hematuria.
Understand the principles of management of patients with hematuria.

topics.title: Problem-based seminar: bladder outlet obstruction
objectives: Discuss the pathophysiology of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
Explain lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS).
Understand the difference between acute and chronic retention and the implications on management.
Explain the mode of action of main classes of drugs used to treat BPH.
Discuss the indication for surgical intervention in BPH and potential complications.
Obtain consent for TURP.
Discuss digital rectal examination (DRE) findings of benign vs malignant prostate.
Understand the principles of management of bladder outflow obstruction.
